chunks: From him, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Muhammad bin Khalid, from Fazalah bin Ayyub, from Umar bin Aban and Sayf bin Ameerah, from Fuzayl bin Yasaar, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) during an illness that had afflicted him such that nothing remained of him except his head (unaffected). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Fuzayl! I very frequently say: what burden is upon a man whom Allah has caused to recognise this matter (al-wilayah), even were he to be atop a mountain, until death comes to him?'
'O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! The people have taken to the right and to the left, but we and our Shia have been guided to the Straight Path.'

'O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! If the believer were to come to possess what lies between the east and the west, that would be better for him; and if he were to find his limbs cut off, that too would be better for him. O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! Allah does not do with the believer except that which is better for him.'
'O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! Had the world equalled in the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so much as the wing of a mosquito, He would not have given His enemy from it a single sip of water.'
'O Fuzayl bin Yasaar! The one whose concern is a single concern — Allah suffices his concern; and the one whose concern scatters into every valley — Allah does not care in which valley he perishes.'

key_terms.الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ: The Straight Path — the path of divine guidance upon which the Imam and his Shia have been established, in contrast to those who deviate to the right or to the left
key_terms.جَنَاحَ بَعُوضَةٍ: Wing of a mosquito — a metaphor conveying the extreme insignificance and worthlessness of the worldly life in the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic
key_terms.عَدُوَّهُ: His enemy — one who stands as an enemy to Allah; the point being that even a single sip of water from this world would be withheld from such a one if the world held any worth before Allah
key_terms.عَرَّفَهُ اللَّهُ: Whom Allah has caused to recognise — divine-given recognition (ma'rifah) of the Imamate and wilayah, indicating that such knowledge is a bestowal from Allah rather than mere human acquisition
key_terms.مُقَطَّعاً أَعْضَاؤُهُ: His limbs cut off — a vivid expression of extreme physical suffering and trial, used to illustrate that any condition in which Allah places the believer is ultimately for his benefit
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرَ: This matter — a technical phrase referring to the wilayah and Imamate of the Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them), recognition of which is deemed sufficient for the believer's salvation
key_terms.هَمُّهُ: His concern/preoccupation — the orientation of one's heart and intention; when singular and directed toward Allah it earns divine sufficiency, when scattered it earns divine neglect

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teach Fuzayl bin Yasaar about the value of recognising the Imamate, the worthlessness of the world, and the importance of singular concern?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), speaking from his sickbed to Fuzayl bin Yasaar, delivers five interconnected counsels: the sufficiency of recognising the Imamate (wilayah) for a believer's salvation regardless of worldly circumstances; the guidance of the Imam and his Shia to the Straight Path while others stray; Allah's exclusive beneficence toward the believer in every condition; the utter worthlessness of this world in Allah's sight; and the divine care granted to the one who directs his heart with singular purpose toward Allah, contrasted with the abandonment of one whose concern is fragmented across worldly preoccupations.
